history.p: August Bournonville got his inspiration for "Thrymskviden" mainly from F.L. Liebenberg's edition of Adam Oehlenschläger's "Nordens Guder". He started working on the ballet in January 1867 and contacted Hartmann in late February. From then on they worked closely together as had been the case with "Valkyrien" (HartW 7), even though the ballet was not officially accepted by the director of The Royal Theatre until 8 February. The costs of sets and costumes were so high that the director recommended that they were divided over two seasons. This was against Bournonville's wish that the first performance should take place in December 1867; unfortunately Hartmann was unable to finish his very complicated score till that time and he did not end-date it until 15 February 1868 - a week before the premiere. After 7 October 1868 the ballet was performed without the recited prologue "Nornerne" (The Norns).

physLoc.identifier: C II, 7 Hartmanns Samling 243 (Kapsel Sulamith - Thrymskviden)

annot.p: This score contains Hartmann's introductory music for the recited prologue by H.P. Holst, entitled "Nornerne" (The Norns). A note on p. 9 indicates that the duration of this prologue was 2½ minutes. The score was used for all performances until Hans Beck's revised staging on 13 January 1901. For that production a completely new score was made (DK-Kk, C II, 114), while the present score was transferred to The Royal Library.

physDesc.physMedium: In half binding with black leather spine and corners and marbled sides. On the spine stamped in gold, the monogram of King Christian X and: "I.P.E. / HARTMANN / THRYMS- / KVIDEN / PARTITUR". Written in black ink. Paper: 20 staves. Originally paginated 1-214, but later new pages have been inserted and each stamped with the number of the page (pp. 57-62, 93-96, 99-114, 159-170). The new pages are written on a later paper type and in a different hand. On the title page added in pencil: "Koncertforeningen" and "A 119", being the Archive Number of Koncertforeningen. Letters added in blue crayon. Numbers of the movements added in red crayon and headings added after the new pages have been inserted.

annot.p: The Suite was performed for the first time in Koncertforeningen on Saturday, 20 November 1886 in Casino conducted by Otto Malling, who that same year published an arrangement of the Suite for four-hand piano. The Suite consists of 14 numbers: 1. Nornerne; 2. Vola og Ildaanderne; 3. Sandsernes Prøve; 4.Thors Kamp med Midgaardsormen; 5. Thrym og Thurserne; 6. Frejas Sal; 7. Skirner kommer til Jothunheim; 8. Ved Ægirs Borg; 9. Gudernes Triumfmarsch; 10. Sigyn og Ternerne; 11. Thors Brudefærd i Jothunheim a) Ildaandernes Forberedelse til Festen b) Thors Ankomst (Marsch) c) Bryllupsfesten. Thor fælder Thrym; 12. Taagen letter; 13. Guderne samles til den sidste Kamp; 14. Gimle.

event.desc: Transferred from Koncertforeningens Arkiv (A 119) to Musikforeningens Arkiv (Mf. 1387) and on to The Royal Library

annot.p: The piano score was published by Horneman & Erslev as a serial in "Musikalsk Museum". From March to December 1868, 14 of the 19 numbers were included in vol. 22, nos. 8-12 and vol 23. nos. 1-5. In December 1868, the complete piano score was available and the last five numbers were incorporated in vol. 23, nos. 6-10, which was published between January and May 1869.
